bull.b: Lam combines strong growth with unusually high profitability and cash conversion. TTM free cash flow reached about 86% of net income, giving the company resources to fund research, capacity expansion, shareholder returns and strategic opportunities through the semiconductor cycle.

The installed-base services business provides a steadier revenue stream than new equipment sales and is expanding across upgrades, spares and services. Continued CSBG growth should improve revenue durability, customer retention and cash-flow visibility as Lam’s equipment footprint grows.

AI-related demand is driving investment in compute, memory and storage, while greater device complexity increases etch, deposition and packaging intensity. Lam’s Akara, Aether and advanced-packaging wins position it to capture more spending as chip architectures become increasingly complex.

bear.b: Lam’s equipment sales depend heavily on customers’ capital-expenditure decisions and technology transitions, creating meaningful cycle exposure. Even with strong current demand, a downturn in memory or logic investment could reduce systems revenue, operating leverage and cash generation over the next several quarters.

Capacity bottlenecks can delay customer fab ramps and prevent Lam from converting strong demand into shipments on schedule. Persistent supply-chain and clean-room constraints could defer revenue, complicate operational planning and limit the company’s ability to fully benefit from the projected WFE expansion.

China represented 35% of September-quarter revenue, so weaker domestic customer spending creates a material regional headwind. A lower China contribution can pressure near-term systems growth and customer mix, particularly if spending remains uneven while other mature-node markets recover gradually.
